DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.169_Text: Are you heading to the cavern?
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.84_Text: Are you planning on planting pineapples this Summer?
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.69_Text: As soon as <NPCName>Suki</> was back in town, our parents decided to retire early. They didn’t think the inn had enough work for four people.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.75_Text: As soon as <NPCName>Suki</> was back in town, our parents decided to retire early. They didn’t think the inn had enough work for four people.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.7_Text: Being alone isn't always bad.//Personal space is rarely a thing when you grow up with someone <Italic>sparkly</> like <NPCName>Suki</>.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.104_Text: Brrrr. It’s starting to get cold. I’ll have to do my reading inside soon.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.40_Text: Can you imagine what life is like on Mars? I would love to go there and see it for myself.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.43_Text: Can you imagine what life is like on Mars? I would love to go there and see it for myself.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.180_Text: Can you smell the salt? Hmmm…
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.172_Text: Could be nothing, but who knows…//<portrait=normal>I might see something one of these days and decide for myself.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.166_Text: Did you hear about the light phenomenon over on Turtle Island?
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.162_Text: Did you just have your morning walk too? I like how quiet it is in the morning.//Right before everyone wakes up. It’s just you and the birds.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.93_Text: Do you know what Summer is good for? Spending time outside, eating tons of minced jackfruit pies, going to the beach – all that good stuff.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.152_Text: Don’t even try to tell <NPCName>Suki</> to sit still and work the desk for too long.//She won’t be able to do it.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.95_Text: Easily the best thing about Summer is the abundance of jackfruit. I can make as many minced jackfruit pies as I want!
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.119_Text: Everyone did such a great job yesterday.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.103_Text: Fall is so pretty, isn’t it? Now, if only it were a bit warmer…
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.168_Text: Fancy meeting you here!//<portrait=happy>I only ever see <NPCName>Ben</> and sometimes a monkey or two.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.32_Text: Ha ha! It IS Monday. Too early to tell, huh?
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.74_Text: He sure is dedicated. <NPCName>Rafael</> visits <NPCName>Valentina</> on weekends and makes sure she’s all right.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.36_Text: Here’s a way to improve the community. The library should get more books about extraterrestrial life.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.44_Text: Here’s a way to improve the community. The library should get more books about extraterrestrial life.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.50_Text: Here’s a way to improve the community. The library should get more books about extraterrestrial life.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.170_Text: Hmm… I think I’ll walk through town on my way home.//<portrait=normal>I have to make a quick stop at the library.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.31_Text: How’s your week been so far?
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.33_Text: I <Italic>did</> take some questionable courses in university.//<portrait=normal>But actually, those classes were the most fun. Looking back, that should have been my major.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.109_Text: I asked my parents <Italic>and</> <NPCName>Suki</> if we could just close the inn for Winter, but they shot me down. Many times.//<portrait=annoyed>You think a broken air conditioner is a problem, wait until you deal with a guest complaining about the heater.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.60_Text: I could be wrong… But I’m keeping my mind open.//<portrait=happy>Let’s see where it gets me.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.131_Text: I couldn’t get to sleep until 1 am. I might have had too much caffeine yesterday.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.165_Text: I didn’t know then that she was going to install drills around the island…//She was always very secretive. Never really looked like a tourist, either.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.167_Text: I do like to read about odd phenomena all over the world.//<portrait=surprised>It fascinates me.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.61_Text: I don’t see why I should buy my own camera.//I don't want to spend money on a camera when I can just borrow <NPCName>Macy</>’s.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.67_Text: I don’t see why I should buy my own camera.//I don't want to spend money on a camera when I can just borrow <NPCName>Macy</>’s.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.39_Text: I don’t think we’re alone in the universe…//I’ve read some interesting theories.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.42_Text: I don’t think we’re alone in the universe…//I’ve read some interesting theories.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.90_Text: I don’t usually love the color pink, but I make an exception for cherry blossoms.//<portrait=happy>They’re just so beautiful.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.130_Text: I had my green tea too late today.//<portrait=sad>I don’t think I’ll be able to sleep tonight…
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.124_Text: I have to start working on a new marketing plan for Winter…
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.163_Text: I have to work today. I’m going straight to the inn after this.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.140_Text: I hope it doesn’t turn into a storm like last time! We can’t afford to install a new heating system every Winter.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.146_Text: I just updated our point-of-sale system. Let’s see how it works!
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.132_Text: I like dinner parties, but sometimes people can wear you out…
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.115_Text: I love seeing all these pretty Summer flowers around the island.//Diversity is beautiful, isn’t it?
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.100_Text: I love seeing the daisies popping up everywhere. It practically screams Summer.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.123_Text: I love walking through the leaves. Do you ever do that?
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.155_Text: I meant, like, <NPCName>Luke</>  for instance. He could rent some space over there, by the door, and sell electronics.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.137_Text: I see you don’t mind it either…
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.121_Text: I should head to <NPCName>Ben’s</> next week. I need to catch him before he leaves for his trip.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.9_Text: I sometimes wonder if running this inn is the right move for me.//I don't know...
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.154_Text: I think it may be a good idea to rent out sales space in the lobby.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.99_Text: I wish <NPCName>Noah</> would come to the forest with me to help with my research, but he just wants to stay at the beach all day.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.120_Text: I wonder if <NPCName>Ben</> has left on his trip yet…
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.178_Text: I wonder if the library has any new books. I’ve been reading the same old books.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.114_Text: If I ever leave this town, the festival would be one thing that I’d miss.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.141_Text: If this Winter gets any colder, I’m afraid we’ll start losing business.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.176_Text: If you're interested in alien, you should read this book by Professor Kiep.//He has interesting theories about ET intelligence. I read it back in university...
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.41_Text: If you’re not a caffeine person, a quick jog does the trick when you need to wake up.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.133_Text: Is it too early to say Happy New Year?
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.1_Text: Is that… Is that you, <PlayerName>$player</>?//<portrait=surprised>Wow! I almost didn’t recognize you in that getup.//<portrait=normal>Oh, so you’re the one moving into the lot, huh? That would explain the outfit.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.112_Text: It can be a bit of a bummer to have a birthday so close to a festival, but our parents made sure we didn’t feel left out when we were younger.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.72_Text: It’s a bit hard to sort through them all. If only there were a filter that showed just certain publications…
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.54_Text: It’s all <NPCName>Suki</>’s idea, to tell you the truth.//<portrait=normal>If it were up to me, I’d just leave the sheets beige.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.64_Text: It’s all <NPCName>Suki</>’s idea, to tell you the truth.//<portrait=normal>If it were up to me, I’d just leave the sheets beige.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.97_Text: It’s easier to do my…research in Summer.//I can stay out longer to see if there’s anything strange on the island.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.98_Text: It’s nice to see the community come together. It’s one of the reasons I love the Beach Cleanup Festival.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.27_Text: It’s nice to see you here, <PlayerName>$player</>.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.14_Text: It’s pretty fair, I think… Right?
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.19_Text: It’s pretty fair, I think… Right?//<portrait=sad>Maybe she doesn’t see it that way...//<portrait=sad>I mean, she does a lot of the cooking, but she doesn’t seem to mind. So don’t you think that’s fair?
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.173_Text: It’s such a different vibe in here compared to the inn.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.102_Text: It’s the last week of Fall, and do you know what that means?//<portrait=annoyed>We have to prepare the inn for Winter. Ugh.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.110_Text: I’d close the inn all Winter if it were up to me. But we can’t. Something about being the only inn in town. Ugh.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.181_Text: I’ll head back to the inn soon. I just wanna get some new books first at the library.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.94_Text: I’ll read anywhere, but there’s something about reading outside in the Summer sun that’s more relaxing.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.147_Text: I’m a little busy right now…
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.96_Text: I’m excited about the Beach Cleanup Festival later this season. Are you?
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.88_Text: I’m glad I made it through another Winter.//<portrait=happy>Now I can look forward to Summer!
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.143_Text: I’m going to put all the extra blankets up front. In case any of our guests need one.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.148_Text: I’m gonna get ready for bed, then read for a bit…
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.89_Text: I’m just counting the days until Summer is here, <PlayerName>$player</>.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.111_Text: I’m looking forward to the New Year’s Eve Festival. It’s so fun and festive, but it also means Winter is officially over.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.179_Text: I’m not being fair. It’s my own fault because I like to reread the same old books.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.47_Text: I’m not doing anything today.//<portrait=happy>Fun, fun!
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.24_Text: I’m pretty much free today. I usually pay the bills on Wednesdays…//That way, I can make sure that we don’t double pay.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.86_Text: I’m so happy Spring is almost over, because it means Summer is right around the corner. I love the longer days!
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.34_Text: I’m sure I’m not the first person who picked the wrong major, though.//<portrait=annoyed>By the way, who told you all this?
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.22_Text: I’ve got a few tips for you. I’ve lived by the beach my whole life, so I know that sometimes you can find rare seashells.//<portrait=happy>I’m talking rare as in expensive!
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.28_Text: I’ve got a few tips for you. I’ve lived by the beach my whole life, so I know that sometimes you can find rare seashells.//<portrait=happy>I’m talking rare as in expensive!
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.49_Text: Just keep in mind that if you like collecting seashells, keep an eye out for them at the beach!
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.151_Text: Just trying to respond to online reviewers. Then I’m going to manage our social media marketing.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.91_Text: Living with <NPCName>Suki</> in Spring has pros and cons.//<portrait=happy>Pro: I barely have to clean anything, because she goes on a cleaning spree.//<portrait=annoyed>Con: She’s even more overbearing and annoying than usual.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.157_Text: Looking for one of our guests, <PlayerName>$player</>?//<portrait=happy>You don’t need my permission. Go ahead and find them.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.116_Text: Make sure to use enough sunscreen for the beach cleanup tomorrow, <PlayerName>$player</>. We’ll be in the sun the whole day.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.136_Text: Meh… A little rain is fine with me…
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.65_Text: Morning jogs can be fun, especially with a partner.//Don’t brush it off just yet. Give it a try!
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.171_Text: My granddad told me that his friend saw a bright green light deep in the forest. He was pretty sure it was an alien spaceship.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.30_Text: Neither <NPCName>Suki</> nor I knew what to do when we first started running Coral Inn. Ha ha. But yeah, it takes a lot to run an inn.//I’m sure it’s nothing compared to running a farm, though.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.128_Text: Nope! I’m not doing that. Thankfully, he changed his mind.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.3_Text: Oh, hello there. It's good to see you here.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.79_Text: Oh, you didn’t find any, you said?//<portrait=normal>Animals might have eaten them already. But have you tried by the river in the forest?
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.81_Text: Oh, you didn’t find any, you said?//<portrait=normal>Animals might have eaten them already. But have you tried by the river in the forest?
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.83_Text: On my morning walk the other day, I saw people gathering bamboo shoots near the lake.//You should check it out.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.160_Text: Once you get to know them better, maybe they’ll let you in their room.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.20_Text: One of my hobbies is definitely reading!//What about you? What do you like to do in your spare time?
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.156_Text: Or – oh! The vineyard! They could sell wine here.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.26_Text: Our kitchen is free to use! It’s included in the room rate.//<portrait=normal>Guests can use our kitchen and anything we put out in the lobby.//But you knew that. You stayed in our inn that summer.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.6_Text: People like to dismiss things they can't see.//What's the fun in that?
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.2_Text: Right. It’s not just the town, you know. The inn isn’t as busy as it used to be.//Hopefully, with you moving in…it’s a sign of something good.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.174_Text: Some people have claimed to see a figure over the lake…//<portrait=happy>The elders call it the Goddess…
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.150_Text: Someone on the internet named Sarahhh with three H’s said that she loved the inn! And couldn’t wait to come back.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.63_Text: Sometimes we dye our sheets different colors to brighten things up…
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.53_Text: Sometimes we dye our sheets different colors to brighten things up…//That way they look new.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.159_Text: Sorry, I can’t open any locked doors for you. If it’s closed, there’s nothing I can help you with.//I guess my best advice is just to talk to the guest.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.92_Text: Summer, finally! Now I can read outside as much as I want.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.57_Text: The 10-year-old me was much more adventurous than adult me.//Now, I like to keep things plain and beige.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.77_Text: The cherry blossoms look beautiful this time of year.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.129_Text: The inn got a bad review last year. A couple complained about the broken heater in their room. So we have to make sure it’s working this year.//<portrait=sad>It could be bad for business otherwise.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.17_Text: The inn usually gets more guests during festivals.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.71_Text: The internet has way too many poorly sourced articles about flying saucers… Hmm…
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.122_Text: The leaves were crunchy on my walk this morning.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.16_Text: The mayor is always watching the economy.//He gets excited about the analysis when we go over what we learned in the past season and all that.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.108_Text: The only good thing about Winter is it’s when our birthday is.//<portrait=annoyed>Everything else I can do without.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.113_Text: The snow is pretty, I’ll admit. But does it have to be so cold?
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.58_Text: The universe is so big, don’t you think?//<portrait=happy>I mean, look at Earth. We haven’t even fully explored it yet.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.48_Text: There is this magnificent rainbow seashell one time that <NPCName>Valentina</> brought home.//<portrait=surprised>Have you seen one of those?//<portrait=normal>Oh, it was so beautiful. I’m pretty sure it would sell for a lot too.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.117_Text: There’s a swimming contest too.//<NPCName>Sunny’s</> going to be the winner again, I bet. Ha ha!
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.87_Text: There’s something cheerful about the flowers in Spring. I know <NPCName>Suki</> can’t get enough of them.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.125_Text: They give out free mooncakes at the Harvest Festival.//They’re <NPCName>Betty’s</>, so they’re good, for sure!
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.85_Text: They’re all right. I was just curious…//But I heard that <NPCName>Joko</> loves pineapples. One time he gave us some as a souvenir from his trip.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.25_Text: Think of it this way, the more people that are allowed access to paying the bills, the more chance that there’ll be mistakes – overpaying, missing invoices, all that.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.78_Text: This time of year, you can find fresh wasabi by the river…
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.80_Text: This time of year, you can find fresh wasabi by the river…
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.38_Text: Uh-uh. Not just me… Let me see… Hmm… <NPCName>Noah</>…and, um…
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.46_Text: Uh-uh. Not just me… Let me see… Hmm… <NPCName>Noah</>…and, um…
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.52_Text: Uh-uh. Not just me… Let me see… Hmm… <NPCName>Noah</>…and, um…
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.15_Text: We keep track of guests daily and run an analysis at the end of the season.//That's how we're taught by our parents.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.149_Text: We offer wine in the evening and a fresh fruit bar in the morning…//<portrait=happy>I think that should be enough, don’t you?
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.59_Text: We seem to keep finding new species of animals… On land, in the ocean! Ancient fish. Gosh.//<portrait=surprised>What else is out there?!//<portrait=happy>Could there be life on other planets? I think so.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.56_Text: When we were kids, <NPCName>Suki</> and I used to dress the same to confuse our friends. It didn’t always work, because we aren’t identical, but when it did, it was great!
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.107_Text: When will this Winter be over?
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.177_Text: Who orders the books inside the library, I wonder?//There are way too many cookbooks.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.101_Text: Why can’t Summer be longer? I haven’t finished my reading yet!
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.23_Text: Yeah! There are plenty of rare, pretty shells on our beach. Kids love collecting them.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.29_Text: Yeah! There are plenty of rare, pretty shells on our beach. Kids love collecting them.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.161_Text: Yes? I don’t want to be rude, but I’m a little too tired to chat…
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.66_Text: You could say that about pretty much anything, though, huh?
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.70_Text: You see, my sis used to live in Labuan Bajo, the little town on the other side of Coral Island, with her ex-husband. But since the, errr, separation, she moved back here.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.76_Text: You see, my sis used to live in Labuan Bajo, the little town on the other side of Coral Island, with her ex-husband. But since the, errr, separation, she moved back here.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.142_Text: …I hope it doesn’t get to that point.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.37_Text: …Just saying. Some people are interested in that stuff, you know.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.45_Text: …Just saying. Some people are interested in that stuff, you know.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.51_Text: …Just saying. Some people are interested in that stuff, you know.
DT_Dialogue_Merfolk_Test.175_Text: …What if…//<portrait=annoyed>What if she’s not a spiritual figure like the locals believe, but actually from another planet?!

DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.19_Text: <NPCName>Randy</> asked me to collect some articles for the kids. Additional reading and such.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.22_Text: <NPCName>Scott</> doesn’t work on weekends.//Honestly, I don’t think he needs to!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.211_Text: <NpcName>Suki</> and I made sure to bring something for <NpcName>Mr. Takeba</>.//<portrait=concerned>He lives alone, and with all the cleaning up he’s doing to this place, I thought it was the least we could do.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.148_Text: <PlayerName>$player</>… Do you think I talk about books too much?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.68_Text: A lot of people get the sniffles this time of year.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.64_Text: A steaming cup of coffee or tea, something to write with, the snow fluttering, and the fireplace roaring…//<portrait=blushing>Doesn’t that sound great?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.192_Text: Ah! <PlayerName>$player</>, you cultured starling! I must recommend you read <Italic>The Hearth Saga</>.//<portrait=normal>First ten pages, and I’m hooked!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.60_Text: Ah, dear Fall. How I’ve missed you.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.183_Text: All is good right now.//I’ve spoken to both <NpcName>Joko</> and <NpcName>Rafael</> about these issues as well.//<portrait=normal>You know, get them ready if anything were to go south.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.188_Text: Apparently, these Giants were small.//They were named for their big, giving hearts… Oh, too out there?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.36_Text: Are we finally going to discuss <Italic>The Tale of Dulcans</>?//<portrait=normal>Have you finished reading the series yet?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.100_Text: Are you looking for a specific book?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.42_Text: Are you planting any melons on your farm?//Oh, right! Melons are a Summer crop, aren’t they?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.94_Text: Because it sure does feel like it to me.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.13_Text: Biology has always interested me, especially wildlife.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.212_Text: But she keeps giving him green smoothies.//They’re unopened in his fridge. I don’t think <NpcName>Mr. Takeba</> likes them very much.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.154_Text: But, I'll miss the twinkle of the snow...
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.204_Text: Can I help you with something, <PlayerName>$player</>?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.156_Text: Can you imagine being on the front line of current world affairs and getting to report on them?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.116_Text: Cooking can be fun. You can get all the fancy gadgets and try out new recipes.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.81_Text: Do I do things differently in Winter?//Hmm, good question.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.93_Text: Does it feel like it storms more in Spring?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.95_Text: Does it feel like it storms more in Summer?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.103_Text: Don’t you just love the smell of old books?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.132_Text: Earlier, I spotted some crows near your farm.//I hope you have scarecrows, <PlayerName>$player</>. Those birds eat crops, after all.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.147_Text: Even crows! They get a bad rap, but they’re fascinating, intelligent creatures.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.43_Text: Every Spring, I always think of poor <NPCName>Charles</>. He gets a case of the sneezes as soon as the flowers start to bloom.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.168_Text: Finished reading a murder mystery last night. Bad idea to stay up for that one.//<portrait=annoyed>I couldn’t sleep until past midnight. Kept thinking I heard something in the kitchen or whatnot…
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.20_Text: First editions are incredibly valuable! Well, to me, anyway. Generally, that’s where the author’s original ideas shine the brightest…alongside the typos.//<portrait=happy>Heh heh!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.174_Text: Good thing my house isn’t far from work, because I don’t think I could walk very far in these shoes.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.165_Text: Hanging out with you is fun.//You seem well read, and that’s really awesome.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.85_Text: Have you noticed the weather channel isn’t always accurate?//It makes it hard to plan my days out.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.125_Text: Have you read anything interesting lately, <PlayerName>$player</>?//My book list is always open for recommendations.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.201_Text: Hey, <PlayerName>$player</>, you look cute! Going somewhere?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.146_Text: Hmm… After giving it some thought, I don’t think I have a favorite bird.//<portrait=normal>I love all birds equally!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.10_Text: Hmm… I think I’ll go to the forest to gather some fresh fruit on Thursday.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.195_Text: How are you today, my glistening dragonfly?//<portrait=normal>Is there anything I can do for you?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.17_Text: How’s life at the farm, you adventurous sword-toting eagle?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.106_Text: How’s your lizard knowledge, <PlayerName>$player</>? Tin hasn’t been showing up much lately.//I’m getting a little worried.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.123_Text: How’s your week shaping up, you magnificent monarch of productivity?//<portrait=happy>Good? Good!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.194_Text: I always love to pass by your farm and see it thriving. You should be proud, <PlayerName>$player</>!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.71_Text: I avoid the beach during Summer because the heat can be too much for me.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.76_Text: I avoid the beach during Summer because the heat can be too much for me.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.46_Text: I can feel the air slowly warming up.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.189_Text: I can just talk and talk and talk to you, you effervescent lark.//<portrait=blushing>And you’re cute too.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.96_Text: I can't be the only one who thinks that, right?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.181_Text: I can’t legally drive without them.//Not that I drive, though.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.177_Text: I can’t see myself being a full-time writer…//<portrait=normal>I like my library job so much I can’t see myself leaving it.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.88_Text: I don’t feel like going anywhere today.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.151_Text: I don’t go to the forest much.//I suppose I’m not much of a hiker.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.127_Text: I don’t often sort my recyclables, though.//<portrait=normal>I’ll make a point to do it when the recycling center is fixed up.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.53_Text: I feel like I romanticize Fall a bit too much.//<portrait=blushing>But don’t you agree there’s something beautiful about writing a novel as the leaves fall around you?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.166_Text: I feel the need to say this out loud. Here goes nothing… Finishing a good book stresses me out. There.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.108_Text: I get here before 10 am almost every day. I like to be punctual.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.208_Text: I got all my documents for the upcoming Beach Cleanup Festival.//I need to hire the Sanchez brothers to help us set up the decorations.//<portrait=happy>I’ll talk to them tomorrow.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.82_Text: I guess not really.//<portrait=normal>I love my library life, but I do enjoy the occasional beach visit too.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.138_Text: I have a good life, all things considered.//I want for very little.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.18_Text: I help the mayor as much as I can with festivals, fairs, and such.//I wish there were more ways to serve our sweet town…
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.74_Text: I hope <NPCName>Sam</> has blueberries. I’m craving some Summer fruit pies!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.87_Text: I hope it stops raining soon.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.137_Text: I know I talk a lot about birds, but I’m fond of butterflies as well.//<portrait=happy>All lovely winged creatures captivate me!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.6_Text: I like hanging out at work, so I usually stay here until I get sleepy.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.128_Text: I like to start the day slowly with a book and a warm mug of coffee.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.33_Text: I like to think of myself as the captain of the library and museum ship here in town.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.130_Text: I love restoring books in my spare time.//Making covers, taking care of old books… Little things like that make my week.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.25_Text: I love worn-out books. To me, they speak of love and appreciation.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.75_Text: I love writing and reading. Sucker for romance fiction here, but I’ll read anything.//<portrait=normal>A good book is a good book.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.153_Text: I must say, I’m counting the days until Spring.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.161_Text: I need to find time to write this weekend… Humph.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.70_Text: I need to get my Summer reading ready!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.28_Text: I once read that some plants survive two seasons…//That must be very economical for business, I would think. Less money spent on seeds.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.84_Text: I plan to channel today's rain into a writing marathon.//<portrait=normal>It makes me feel contemplative.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.72_Text: I prefer the beach in Winter, to be honest… Thick jacket and chilly wind.//Best combo.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.77_Text: I prefer the beach in Winter, to be honest… Thick jacket and chilly wind.//Best combo.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.152_Text: I prefer to walk on proper roads.//But in your line of work, walking through the dirt seems unavoidable!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.118_Text: I should go home soon. I need time to make dinner.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.160_Text: I still have some donated books in the back that need sorting.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.143_Text: I suppose you know how it feels to yearn for a change of pace.//You left everything behind to come here, after all.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.14_Text: I take Thursdays off.//I’ll be at the library first thing tomorrow morning.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.122_Text: I tell you, when I see a beat-up first edition in need of care, it makes my week.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.203_Text: I want nothing more than to curl up with a hot drink and a good book tonight…//Ah… Winter nights.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.209_Text: I was just telling <NpcName>Suki</> about the books I’ve been reading… There’s this one particular horror novel. I can’t stand it.//<NpcName>Suki</> doesn’t mind spoilers, ‘cos they’re not her type of books anyway.//She probably won’t read them.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.159_Text: I was minding my own business, bird-watching and whatnot.//<portrait=angry>I refuse to wear bug repellent. I do… I won’t do it.//If it costs me my body, then so be it.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.158_Text: I was stung by a bug yesterday. Don’t know what it was. All of a sudden, I felt my hand burning…//Thankfully, I was just in front of my house, so I went in and took care of it right away.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.157_Text: I wish I could do that kind of journalism.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.63_Text: I wonder how many great authors write in the dead of Winter.//It feels like the perfect season for writing. I prefer writing in Fall myself, though.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.73_Text: I wonder if <NPCName>Sam</>’s is open today. I’m running out of milk and fruit.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.98_Text: I wonder if <NPCName>Sam</>’s is open today. I’m running out of milk and fruit.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.37_Text: I'm thinking about trying diving tomorrow, unless I get too caught up watching the birds.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.49_Text: I've been thinking about baking some cookies for the kids at the library, instead of getting them from <NPCName>Sam</>'s.//<portrait=normal>It's a fun idea but in this heat, I don’t think it’s worth the money saved, right?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.29_Text: If you have anything to donate, please send it over to the museum. We have a donation box there.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.21_Text: Imagine, being the first to explore the undiscovered territories of an author's mind...
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.185_Text: Investigative journalism must be thrilling. To be on the front line of world affairs, to pull back the curtain for the public…//<portrait=sad>What I wouldn’t give.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.47_Text: Is it too early to start looking for melons at <NPCName>Sam</>’s? Hmm…
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.112_Text: It feels too cold to go to the beach. I think I’ll go home after this.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.169_Text: It was probably just the wind, right? It was pretty windy last night.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.145_Text: It’s even worse when it seems like the series will never be finished… What do I do then?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.210_Text: It’s nice here, isn’t it? Away from the town…
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.66_Text: It’s the Cherry Blossom Festival tomorrow.//I think I’ll bring some vegetables… I’m not sure yet.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.179_Text: It’s the little things in life that matter, right?//<portrait=surprised>That’s the spirit! You sparkly butterfly!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.54_Text: I’m always inspired to write more in Fall. I wonder why that is…
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.55_Text: I’m craving some ramen right now. Any kind of ramen. Mmm…
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.171_Text: I’m getting my reading bingo ready for Fall.//I’m going to start with a murder mystery! It’s a classic reread from my favorite mystery author, Agatha Christine. Oh, so excited!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.12_Text: I’m grateful for all the donations the library receives. Not just books, you know. We get plenty of money as well.//<portrait=normal>Some donations even come in from neighboring islands.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.114_Text: I’m here to pick up some fresh fish for dinner.//I’m thinking about cooking fish tacos tonight… Hmm?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.121_Text: I’m hoping we get more first editions!//<portrait=normal>Book restoration is a hobby of mine.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.67_Text: I’m like a well-prepared scout.//I got my flu shot early this year, so I’m fully equipped for the sniffle season.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.206_Text: I’m nervous about the upcoming Tree Planting Festival… I’m scared we may not all fit in the boat.//Let’s hope for the best!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.207_Text: I’m so glad the Tree Planting Festival is behind us.//Aside from a couple of people getting seasick, I thought it went pretty well. No boat issues… Nothing!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.44_Text: I’m starting to see a lot more lizards out. Even my lizard, Tin, is a lot more active now.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.140_Text: I’m sure a lot of our customs will become clearer with them in mind!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.56_Text: I’ve been communicating a lot with Beluga Bay, since we’re the one hosting the Harvest Festival.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.62_Text: I’ve been eating too much ramen, but I can’t help myself!//<portrait=happy>I love some soupy goodness in the frigid Winter.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.187_Text: I’ve been investigating the old legends of this island, and I found some incredible things! Prepare yourself.//<portrait=surprised>Giants used to live here! Isn’t that amazing?!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.162_Text: I’ve been putting it off all week.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.196_Text: I’ve been submitting articles to online publications on a pretty consistent basis.//<portrait=normal>Not much has come of it yet.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.178_Text: I’ve been submitting articles to online publications on a pretty consistent basis.//<portrait=normal>There hasn’t been much income from it yet, but I get a lot of satisfaction writing about things I care about.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.39_Text: I’ve been trying to write one article the whole day.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.202_Text: I’ve read more than my fair share of romance novels, you know.//<portrait=blushing>And now I feel like I’m living in one!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.149_Text: I… Hmm. No, I suppose I don’t. My apologies for bothering you.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.141_Text: Let me know if you ever want a book recommendation.//<portrait=normal>I often suggest books to townsfolk!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.149_Special: Maybe a little. Don’t you have more to say?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.176_Text: Maybe my feet hurt because I’ve been standing too much today.//It could also be that I need a new pair of shoes.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.57_Text: Mayor <NPCName>Connor</> is really itching to win the harvest display this year…and me too!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.40_Text: My brain feels like it's stuck in a traffic jam today.//Can't find a worthwhile thought to save my life.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.129_Text: My favorite way to kickstart the day is with a captivating book and a steaming mug of ambition... I mean coffee!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.175_Text: My feet hurt.//<portrait=confused>I think I’ve spent too long standing…
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.4_Text: Nah, not today. Maybe I’ll do it once the recycling center is fixed up.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.150_Special: No. It makes you happy, so it’s not too much.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.61_Text: Now it’s Winter, I can finally relax a bit.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.142_Text: Now, what’s a free-roaming butterfly like you doing in here, <PlayerName>$player</>?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.15_Text: Oh gosh… Sometimes I read for too long. Then I get that dizzy feeling when I stand up… Do you know what I’m talking about?//<portrait=concerned>Good thing my housemate is a doctor.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.69_Text: Oh my! Is this the last week of Spring already?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.170_Text: Oh no! Summer is literally so close. I haven’t set up my reading bingo yet. What should I do, magnificent blue grasshopper?//I know, I know! I need to start tonight, or else it’ll be too late.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.27_Text: Oh! An endless sea of books to sail and just a tiny ship of time.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.133_Text: Oh! I also saw some parrots!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.11_Text: Oh! Or maybe I should transform into a beach-loving pelican!//Pack a lunch, grab some books, and bask in the glory of the sun... decisions, decisions.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.180_Text: Oh! You elegant, gullible, slimy cocoon. My glasses aren’t fake.//<portrait=normal>They’re real. I have bad eyesight, and my eyes are too dry for contacts.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.144_Text: Once in a while, I get invested in a series of novels, only to find the author hasn’t completed it.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.102_Text: Once you donate a certain number of items, you’re welcome to collect your reward.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.30_Text: Once you put a donation in the box, I file all the information before we start the inspection process. When that’s done, <NPCName>Scott</> takes care of the rest.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.115_Text: Or I could just buy a premade meal.//It’s much easier, and I know it’ll be good. Guaranteed.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.163_Text: Part of being a journalist is being thorough in your investigations.//Some of the topics I pick may not pan out, but the journey of discovery is the most important thing.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.83_Text: Please be careful with the books here.//Some of them are very old and delicate, so wet hands can damage them.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.50_Text: Pufferfish is going to have a stand at this year’s Beach Cleanup Festival. *sighs* It’s kind of hard to say no to them.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.124_Text: Reading truly is a marvel. How else can we connect so intimately with people across time?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.24_Text: Romance novels are my ultimate guilty pleasure. The good ones can really draw you in emotionally.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.16_Text: She doesn’t give me a discount at the clinic, though.//Should I ask for it?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.3_Text: Should I sort my recyclables, you think?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.197_Text: Still, I get a lot of satisfaction from writing about something that matters to me.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.48_Text: Summer can get pretty stuffy.//<portrait=happy>Thankfully, I live in Garden Lane. It’s so green and lush. Once you open the window – wah… The breeze is amazing!//<portrait=normal>It’s the base camp for bugs, though. I bet you could catch a lot of them there, am I right?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.113_Text: Thankfully, it’s nice and warm in here.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.150_Text: That’s so sweet of you to say! Thank you. I needed to hear that.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.26_Text: That’s what books aspire to, right? To be read over and over again by many people.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.41_Text: The Cherry Blossom Festival always fills me with joy.//<portrait=normal>It's the blooming trees, the community spirit...it's just perfect.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.58_Text: The Harvest Festival is one of the more complicated festivals to set up, but I always have so much fun while it’s happening.//<portrait=happy>It feels like a reward for all the hard work!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.205_Text: The Harvest Festival was a blast! I’m glad the community had fun.//The Sanchez brothers helped us set up the decorations. I don’t know what I’d do without them.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.65_Text: The best thing about having a doctor as a roommate is I can just ask her to do my checkups at home.//<portrait=normal>I still have to pay her, though, which is fair enough.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.101_Text: The farming books are over there.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.52_Text: The grass is looking kind of sad, isn’t it? That lot next to my house looks so dry.//So yellow… Poor things.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.191_Text: The library can be somewhat lonesome. Thank you for visiting, <PlayerName>$player</>.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.193_Text: The library has copies you can check out. It’s gripping.//<portrait=normal>I just know you’ll love it!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.109_Text: The lights here are funny. I think the wiring must be old and needs some work.//<portrait=annoyed>Sometimes they go off and on by themselves.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.139_Text: The local legends of this island are rather captivating.//You ought to read up on them, if you haven’t already.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.134_Text: The townsfolk are quite eager to help out around town, especially with changing the seasonal decorations.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.86_Text: The weather channel isn’t always accurate.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.136_Text: This island’s wildlife never ceases to amaze me. So much gorgeous fauna!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.9_Text: This job is like winning the lottery for a bookworm like me.//<portrait=normal>I get to devour novels while making sure they're well-organized. A double treat!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.135_Text: Though I must admit, the decorations are my favorite part too!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.186_Text: Though investigative journalism sounds thrilling, it also sounds really scary. Like really, really…//<portrait=concerned>To be on the front line of world affairs, to pull back the curtain for the public…//I don’t know if I’d have it in me.//…
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.38_Text: Time certainly flies when you’re having fun.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.107_Text: Tin isn’t exactly a pet, more of a spontaneous lizard visitor who likes to hang out with me.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.45_Text: Tin likes to be out and about. He rarely stays inside his little glass room, that one.//An adventurer!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.199_Text: To think, of all the single people in Starlet Town, you chose me!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.97_Text: Today's snowfall is inspiring me to write.//<portrait=normal>It makes me feel contemplative.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.182_Text: Today, I spoke with the mayor about our town.//With Winter coming up, we have to be ready for the Winter Fair, snow storms… Winter stuff like that.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.126_Text: Tomorrow is my recycling day! Scheduling chores helps me remember to do them.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.59_Text: Until we meet again, sweet, sweet Fall air…
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.155_Text: Watch out for caterpillars, <PlayerName>$player</>. Try not to step on them! They’re everywhere.//Be the observant hawk that you are!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.105_Text: We got several donations from <NPCName>Zarah</>.//She worked with us a couple of times to find some lost treasures.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.8_Text: We have a large selection of books here. Feel free to immerse yourself in this ocean of wisdom.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.120_Text: We have a large selection of books here. Take your time browsing!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.131_Text: We have several shelves of first editions here. They’re the library’s most precious assets, at least to me.//<portrait=happy>Some are even signed by the author!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.23_Text: We have the museum under control.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.51_Text: We ran out of melons yesterday. I wonder if <NPCName>Sam</> still has some…
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.167_Text: Well…’cause then, I have to pick a new book to read.//There’s also the worry about whether the new book will be as good as the one I just finished.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.184_Text: What a joy to see you here, <PlayerName>$player</>!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.200_Text: What am I going to do with you, my beautiful lory?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.34_Text: What’s a butterfly like you doing in here, <PlayerName>$player</>?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.35_Text: What’s a butterfly like you doing in here, <PlayerName>$player</>?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.31_Text: When I pass by your farm, I tell you, it's got the best sunset view in town.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.164_Text: When Pufferfish tried to move here, I should have written an article about them and how damaging oil drilling is.//<portrait=concerned>It was a missed opportunity on my part. But maybe it’s not too late.//An article about oil spills might be informative.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.5_Text: When we have a community garden, I’ll plant a lot of flowers.//<portrait=annoyed>Won’t be able to help out with gardening except on Thursdays, though.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.104_Text: When we receive a new shipment of books, I like to do the unpacking myself.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.7_Text: Why would I hang out at home when the library is the heart of Starlet Town? Exactly, there's no reason!
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.1_Text: Yes, <PlayerName>$player</>!//<portrait=normal>I’ve been meaning to meet you. My name is <NPCName>Millie</>.//It’s so exciting to have people moving in.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.99_Text: You can read about fish here. There are plenty of informative books about when to catch them.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.110_Text: You can see all kinds of butterflies and birds from here.
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.172_Text: You look like you’re having a fantastic Sunday, <PlayerName>$player</>!//<portrait=normal>What’s your secret?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.173_Text: You look like you’re having a fantastic Winter, <PlayerName>$player</>!//<portrait=normal>What’s your secret?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.198_Text: You really are lovely, <PlayerName>$player</>. Brave and strong, yet so tender… Ah, how did I get so lucky?
DT_Dialogue_Millie_Production.32_Text: Your farm is like a little gem in our community.//But it's got to be as much work as organizing a town festival!

DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.81_Text: <NPCName>Bree’s</> parties are always so much fun, aren’t they? Nowhere near as much fun as Mother’s, of course. Too bad you haven’t been to any.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.156_Text: <NPCName>Lily</> is a dear friend. She stays at the villa when I’m away. If you want to win brownie points with her, give her omurice.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.63_Text: <NPCName>Walter</> and Father used to take <NPCName>Luke</> and me sailing the first weekend of every Summer.//<portrait=sad>Eventually, we stopped that tradition, and then Father, well…
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.146_Text: Ah, I rarely spend my days at home.//The whole living alone thing gets boring fast, so I come here instead.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.97_Text: Ah, the wind is nice and breezy today!
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.172_Text: Am I interested in anyone here?//Hmm… No. Not really.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.158_Text: Am I really? A smart person? Well, takes one to know one.//I always enjoy my conversations with you, precisely because of that.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.74_Text: Around this time of the year, Mother always made sure we were ready for our annual skiing trip.//<portrait=annoyed>I’m not very good at it… It never really <Italic>hooked</> me, as it were.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.180_Text: Before moving back to Coral Island, I decided it was time for Mother and me to clean up our stuff here.//Then I came here that Summer to pick up some of my antiques and check out the new farmer.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.52_Text: Being caught between two families, two cultures, has always lent a certain...intrigue to my life.//When I was with my mom's side, they would look at me and see Father.//With all the blondes, I was the only one with black hair.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.49_Text: But over the years, I've learned that my unique blend is not a sign of not fitting in, but rather a badge of honor...a testament to the rich tapestry of my existence.//<portrait=happy>After all, what's life without a little spice?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.62_Text: Can’t believe that crybaby grew up to be so tall.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.205_Text: Care to join us, <PlayerName>$Player</>?//I'm just out here soaking up the sun.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.127_Text: Come on! Show me what you’ve got.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.15_Text: Coral Island feels the most like home to me.//I feel like packing up and moving right back in this Winter!
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.125_Text: Did I really call him Dad? Ha! That’s new.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.69_Text: Do you think <NPCName>Luke</> will still let me put flower crowns on him?//<portrait=normal>Probably not, huh?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.157_Text: Don’t tell her I told you that. Take the credit!
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.47_Text: Even though I was born here, darling, Mother hails from an entirely different corner of the world.//Hence, the conundrum...am I truly a Coral Island native?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.29_Text: Falling asleep with my windows open is the best. The sound of the ocean is so relaxing.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.196_Text: Father and I used to sit there, right there near the pool table.//Those are the exact stools Father and I used to sit our <Italic>butts</> on.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.168_Text: Father gave the farm to Mother as a birthday or anniversary gift. I can’t remember which.//<portrait=normal>But at that point, they were fighting a lot, and she thought it was just Father’s way to shut her up.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.120_Text: Father used to bring me here after hours to get a treat.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.182_Text: Father was a good man, <PlayerName>$player</>. But there was a period…umm…toward the end of his life, when he was distant from us.//He got skinnier and skinnier.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.171_Text: Father was a thoughtful man.//He loved her very much.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.66_Text: Father was the one who taught me how to surf and sail. Well…not personally. He was too busy for that.//But he was the one pushing for lessons and camps.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.128_Text: Father would flip if he knew I cut my hair short like this!
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.36_Text: For my seventh birthday, Father got me a small patch of land over on Turtle Island. Our family uses it for berry planting.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.50_Text: Growing up, I often felt like an amalgam of my parents, not quite mirroring either of them.//It made me feel somewhat out of place.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.101_Text: Ha ha ha. Silly, I know.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.28_Text: Ha ha… Never mind. I think I’ve been reading one too many mysteries.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.129_Text: Ha! Kidding. He wouldn’t! Father wouldn’t care. He would literally let me do whatever I wanted… And I did.//Mother was angry every time I threw dinner plates across the table. But not Father.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.169_Text: He was acting very distant, and Mother kept complaining about us never having family dinners anymore.//<portrait=annoyed>It was a mess.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.183_Text: He was so small when he…//We never knew what was wrong with him. Doctors said there was nothing wrong.//<portrait=sad>All the tests were negative. It was heartbreaking to see him that way. Mother and I – we never got our answers.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.155_Text: Hmm… Carries some bad memories too, though.//So, not a very cute time capsule, I suppose.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.18_Text: How are you doing today, Farmer <PlayerName>$player</>?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.112_Text: Humph. Oh well… It’s only water, right? So what if it’s a little muddy?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.116_Text: Humph. Oh well… The rain is only water, right? So what if it’s a little muddy and thundery?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.178_Text: I asked Mother why she never wanted to visit Coral Island. Oh yeah, I did!//She just brushed it off, saying she’d been here her whole adult life, and she’d had enough.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.197_Text: I can’t remember if I turned my TV off before coming here.//Yeah, I did.//Wait… No… Never mind.//<portrait=normal>Maybe I should call it a night. Yeah.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.79_Text: I can’t wait for the New Year’s Eve Festival!//<portrait=normal>I definitely missed it when I moved away.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.90_Text: I could never, anyway. It’s my childhood home. There’s no way I could ever destroy or sell the villa.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.92_Text: I could never, anyway. It’s my childhood home. There’s no way I could ever destroy or sell the villa.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.4_Text: I could sell the whole house, and I swear to you, new things would still keep popping up. Ha!
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.144_Text: I don’t need most of the things here. My family has so much unnecessary stuff.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.9_Text: I don’t need most of the things in my house.//It’d be best for me to rehome the art and the furniture, but it really isn’t that simple.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.135_Text: I don’t see kids building elaborate sandcastles anymore.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.72_Text: I forget how pretty Coral Island is in Autumn. It’s just so picturesque with all the falling leaves.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.46_Text: I get confused when people ask me where I’m from. Coral Island is definitely home to me, so I always tell them that.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.193_Text: I get why people like this place.//It’s so homey here…
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.104_Text: I got my party-planning gene from Mother.//She’d invite everybody on the island for my birthday.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.179_Text: I guess now we know where I got my dramatic gene. Heh!
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.57_Text: I hate Spring cleaning.//<portrait=surprised>I should ask <NPCName>Suki</> to do it. She <Italic>loves</> Spring cleaning.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.34_Text: I hate to call the villa a vacation home, because it’s actually home in my eyes… Not some resort hotel.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.174_Text: I hate to monopolize our conversations. So, please, just stop me when you’ve had enough.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.204_Text: I have a lot of beautiful memories here.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.142_Text: I haven’t spent a Winter here in so long.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.5_Text: I just adore this island. They call themselves “islanders.” Oh, my heart! So adorbs.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.20_Text: I know Mother would tell me to do whatever makes me happy.//But I really don’t want to leave her alone, now that Father is gone.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.148_Text: I learned to sail a long time ago, when I was <NPCName>Valentina’s</> age. Father sent me to a Summer camp where I also learned to scuba dive.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.191_Text: I live way too far from your place. Ugh.//Don’t let it stop you from visiting me, though.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.12_Text: I love the mayor. He’s like a father to me. Always makes sure I feel welcome here.//Like, who do you know with a better heart?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.203_Text: I miss farming with Mother, waking up early and strolling around rows and rows of flowers.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.48_Text: I must confess, there were times growing up when I felt as though I didn't quite match my own reflection in the family portrait.//An artist with mismatched paint, if you will.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.95_Text: I need to pack tomorrow. I’m bringing back some antiques and wine for Mother.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.105_Text: I never really understood why, because honestly, to me, it was more tiring than anything. And I always had to wear some itchy dress. I hated those. The parties, though – They were out of this world.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.32_Text: I should host a dinner party and invite all my friends. Would you come?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.200_Text: I spoke to <NpcName>Raj</> the other day.//They sure know a lot about coffee. I don’t think I understood half the things they said.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.121_Text: I suppose it doesn’t matter how far away I go. I’ll always belong here…
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.133_Text: I suppose it doesn’t matter how far away I go. I’ll always belong here…
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.136_Text: I suppose it may be a different era now.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.58_Text: I tried going into the ocean the other day, and it was still too cold!//<portrait=concerned>Maybe I need to wait a few more days…
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.85_Text: I tried to get Mother to spend Summer here with me. Just this one time, you know. I didn’t want to come alone. But she refused.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.181_Text: I was shocked – amazed – to meet you. You’re so cute.//Took my breath away.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.60_Text: I wonder what <NPCName>Suki</> is up to. Frantically cleaning the inn, probably.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.24_Text: I'm planning a day at the beach tomorrow, perhaps followed by a visit to the Tavern.//<portrait=happy>Will I see you there?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.192_Text: If you get tired, you’re welcome to stay the night. There are extra bedrooms…if you’ll be needing one.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.8_Text: If you see anything you like at the villa, just let me know, darl.//I can probably sell it to you.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.195_Text: In retrospect, I probably wouldn’t have moved back if this island were overrun with drilling sites.//Why would anyone?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.16_Text: Is that impulsive? Maybe I should wait until Spring.//<portrait=annoyed>I need to talk to Mother about it first, anyway… See what she thinks.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.124_Text: It was a really bad habit of his… Overworking himself. Then he would bring me here for father-daughter time to make up for the time he spent working.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.94_Text: It would be such fun to stay for Autumn! But I can’t… Ugh!
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.206_Text: It’s a bit too cold to keep the windows open now.//<portrait=concerned>The ocean wind is strong.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.40_Text: It’s blueberry season! Oh, I would love to visit a berry farm this time of year.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.42_Text: It’s cranberry season! Oh, I would love to visit a berry farm this time of year.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.75_Text: It’s getting cold, isn’t it?//<portrait=annoyed>Remind me again why I decided to move back here.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.118_Text: It’s just a little bit of water.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.153_Text: It’s like we’re good friends or something.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.38_Text: It’s strawberry season! Oh, I would love to visit a berry farm this time of year.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.139_Text: I’d invite you in, but the house still smells a bit musty.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.93_Text: I’ll be here next Summer. Why wouldn’t I be? I’d miss it too much.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.100_Text: I’m afraid if I go to the forest alone, I might get lost and run into one of those monsters.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.21_Text: I’m all she’s got. I feel bad, but I also don’t want to force her to move here with me.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.164_Text: I’m glad your grandparents purchased the farm from my parents.//Because if it weren’t for that… I may never have met you.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.10_Text: I’m heading to Dulca Island for the Autumn.//It’s the best time to visit, if you’re interested… Then I’m probably going to spend Winter with Mother.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.149_Text: I’m not a big diver, but it did add some heft to my college application.//And it comes in handy for conversation at cocktail parties. So, I’m grateful.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.83_Text: I’m not technically new here.//Oh no, no!//My family used to live on Coral Island until Mother decided to leave some time ago.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.71_Text: I’m so <Italic>so</> sad Summer is over. Should I leave town again?//<portrait=happy>Just kidding! I think I’m gonna stay here for a while.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.56_Text: I’m so excited for Summer, darl. It’ll be so much fun!//<portrait=surprised>The food, the swimming, the beach – everything!
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.55_Text: I’m so glad it’s starting to get warmer. I was this close to packing up and moving somewhere else!
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.82_Text: I’m so tempted to spend the Winter somewhere warmer.//<portrait=happy>Want to join me sometime?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.201_Text: I’ve always tried to make it to every festival, even when I didn’t live here.//They’re too precious to miss!
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.190_Text: I’ve heard plenty of theories myself – about my own family.//<portrait=normal>The most absurd one was that Father died from some black magic, and now whatever it was is after Mother. They say that’s why Mother was so “scared” to come back here.//<portrait=annoyed>Foolish! An insensitive take on a tragedy.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.64_Text: Just look around us, darl. You can see why I always come back here in Summer, can’t you?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.173_Text: Let me take that back… There is one person, actually.//A very smart, <Italic>very</> flirty person who piques my interest.//<portrait=happy>Not telling you who…
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.27_Text: Let me tell you something… Sometimes I feel like I’m being watched.//There’s an extra pair of eyes in the villa. I can feel it.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.44_Text: Living at the beach is hard to beat. Falling asleep with my windows open is simply the best.//The sound of the ocean is so relaxing.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.23_Text: Maybe next year. Start off with a clean slate, you know…
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.107_Text: Mother always insisted we go skiing in Winter, because you can do everything else any other time, according to her.//But skiing can only be done in Winter.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.3_Text: Mother is always such a collector. I’m constantly finding new things around the house.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.187_Text: Mother likes to garden. She used to only plant flowers, but sometimes she planted berries for us to harvest during berry season, like now.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.167_Text: Mother was getting too sick to care for the garden.//Father wasn’t in great condition either… It was for the best.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.166_Text: Mr. and Mrs. Dudley don’t work for us anymore. They retired and moved to Beluga Bay.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.35_Text: My childhood friends are all here. This is where my parents had me.//Mother planted flowers in this soil. And Father…//<portrait=annoyed>And Father was laid to rest here.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.123_Text: My dad worked long hours at home, and there was a period when he didn’t come out of his office for days at a time.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.162_Text: My family used to pay some local farmers, Mr. and Mrs. Dudley, to look after the farm with Mother.//Back when she was still healthy…
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.186_Text: My head has gotten so large since I met you. The compliments… They’re gonna get to me, you know.//<portrait=happy>And you do <Italic>not</> want to see the consequences.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.33_Text: My oh my! Darling, you have to come. There will be plenty of food and music… New friends!//<portrait=happy>It’ll be so much fun.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.188_Text: My parents and I would make a day of it.//<portrait=normal>Father would take a day off from his banking job. Just go to the farm, bring some lunch, and harvest all kinds of berries.//Blueberries, blackberries…
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.160_Text: My parents collected antiques from different eras.//That’s how they bonded. Over old, musty decor. Shocking!
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.25_Text: No promises, though. If I get too exhausted, then I’ll just go straight home.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.177_Text: Not to check on the villa, not to visit Father’s grave… Never.//Sometimes, she and <NPCName>Bree</> have lunch together, but never on Coral Island.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.84_Text: Now I spend my Summers here, catching up with old friends…and making new ones along the way.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.184_Text: Oh dear… Thank you. You’re such a flirt.//<portrait=blushing>You don’t look bad yourself. You obviously know that… People must throw themselves at you. I kind of hate it.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.143_Text: Oh gosh, I hope the heat still works.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.115_Text: Oh my! Was that thunder I just heard?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.96_Text: Oh my! What a fun Summer! I just absolutely love it here.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.22_Text: Oh my… I’m debating whether I should move back here this coming Winter or next year.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.11_Text: Oh yes, of course. They call it Fall here, not Autumn, don’t they?//<portrait=normal>It’s the falling leaves season.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.61_Text: Oh, I need to tell you a funny story about <NPCName>Luke</>.//One time, we were hunting for ghosts by that temple near the villa. It was dark, and I sneaked away from him while he walked around the temple.//I hid, and when he noticed I was gone, he kept calling my name over and over again.//<portrait=surprised>So then, I jumped out and scared him! He fell down, and he cried and cried and cried!
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.59_Text: Oh, darl, it’s finally, finally getting warmer. I can feel the Summer vibes just around the corner!
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.78_Text: Oh, darling, how do you stay so active in Winter? It’s so cold!
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.70_Text: Oh, do you happen to grow berries on your farm? I think Autumn is the perfect season for berry picking, don’t you?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.106_Text: Oh, how I miss the sound of waves! I just spend the day curled up under a blanket.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.37_Text: Oh, nothing compared to your farm, doll! A blueberry to a watermelon! My patch of land is as small as my villa.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.117_Text: Oh, this rain isn’t going to stop me from leaving my house.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.189_Text: People are getting creative with stories nowadays. I don’t pay attention to gossip, darl.//I don’t care what people say about why my family left the island.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.19_Text: Remember, I’m rooting for you! Keep it up.//<portrait=normal>I don’t know what I’m rooting for just yet, but I am! Go <PlayerName>$player</>!
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.86_Text: She prefers cold winds, she said. No use trying to talk Mother into anything. Fine by me…
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.108_Text: She’s not wrong, but it doesn’t make it right. I mean, every Winter, <PlayerName>$player</>? Skiing? Come on!
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.87_Text: So, tell me. What have you learned about farming so far?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.138_Text: So, when you were in school, what did you do during your Summer breaks, if not sailing?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.151_Text: So, when you were in school, what did you do during your Summer breaks, if not sailing?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.176_Text: Soon after Father passed away, Mother decided to move our whole life out of here.//She hasn’t returned since.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.54_Text: Spring cleaning is such a pain when you have a big house. It’s even worse when you have a mother who likes to buy so many things. Ugh.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.185_Text: Stop it, you… I just threw something on. Nothing fancy at all.//If you keep complimenting me, I’ll have to put you in my pocket and take you home with me.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.31_Text: Sure, occasionally you get lonely, but sometimes it’s nice to just be by yourself, you know?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.51_Text: Thankfully, none of the people here ever made me feel like my appearance matters too much.//Family gatherings, on the other hand... Let's just say my cousins had a knack for reminding me of my uniqueness.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.165_Text: That farm has the history of both our families in it.//<portrait=happy>It would be interesting to see what it would be like to live there…together.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.202_Text: That’s one of the advantages of having a house here. You can just pop in anytime and stay for the night.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.67_Text: The Beach Cleanup Festival is the main reason I love Summer so much.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.194_Text: The family that used to take care of the farm for us always had the same dinner here, for years.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.199_Text: The flowers here are beautiful. It makes me feel like a fairy when I’m in this garden.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.102_Text: The leaves are solid brown now. It’s a sign the trees will start losing leaves soon.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.113_Text: The one time I’m here, it rains like this.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.109_Text: The one time I’m here, it rains.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.110_Text: The one time I’m here, it rains.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.175_Text: The truth is…it’s hard for me to think clearly when I’m around you.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.89_Text: The villa is too big for me. But I know Mother would be outraged if I swapped it for a modest-sized cabin.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.91_Text: The villa is too big for me. But I know Mother would be outraged if I swapped it for a modest-sized cabin.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.103_Text: The weather has definitely changed, but not enough to need a sweater.//I’m fine, thanks for asking.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.6_Text: The wild jackfruit is so sweet here. If you’re lucky, you might find some massive ones near the river.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.53_Text: Then with Father's family, they would look at me and see Mother.//<portrait=normal>I was like her mirror in how I moved and behaved.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.17_Text: There's a vast collection of art and furniture in my home that I barely use.//<portrait=concerned>I'm considering finding them new homes, but it's not as easy as one might think.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.77_Text: There’s something really beautiful about the beach in Winter, isn’t there?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.99_Text: This may sound a bit silly, but I’m curious about the forest. I heard there are monsters in the cavern.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.119_Text: This place hasn’t changed. I love it.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.14_Text: This place is the best in Summer. Love, love, <Italic>love</> keeping up with my childhood friends!//<portrait=normal>Surfing, staying up, chilling at the beach. What more is there to life?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.145_Text: This stuff is never used. It’s probably bored, sitting around with nobody paying attention to it.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.154_Text: This town is like a cute little time capsule.//Hasn’t changed much since I left. Without a doubt, it carries a lot of memories.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.131_Text: This volleyball court wasn’t here last year. I wonder if this was Pufferfish’s doing as well.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.132_Text: Up for a game of volleyball?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.137_Text: Wait, are you joking? You don’t know how to sail?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.150_Text: Wait, are you joking? You don’t know how to sail?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.152_Text: We always have so much fun together. Did you notice that?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.163_Text: We built the cabin for them to live in, and they kept most of what they earned from the harvest.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.98_Text: We got just what we needed.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.80_Text: We need to keep hydrated, always. Especially in Winter, when it’s dry like this.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.1_Text: Well, hello… Nice to meet you. Call me <NPCName>Nina</>.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.88_Text: What a fun, simple life! I need to get me one of those. Oh, it’s just so tiring to always move from place to place, never feeling at home.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.39_Text: What better way to spend the afternoon than toting around a basketful of berries and fresh flowers?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.41_Text: What better way to spend the afternoon than toting around a basketful of berries and fresh flowers?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.43_Text: What better way to spend the afternoon than toting around a basketful of berries and fresh flowers?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.73_Text: What do you call it, darl, Autumn or Fall?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.198_Text: What do you think about this house?//Do you like it? Should I repaint the walls?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.76_Text: What should I do today?//The cold weather makes me lazy.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.68_Text: When I was younger, Father and Mother took me to the beach almost every single day in Summer.//Father would play with me in the water, and Mother would make banana fritters.//<portrait=happy>We always finished the day with some corn on the cob from the cart. It was so much fun!
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.65_Text: When I was younger, we didn’t always live here. But Father always made sure we came here for Summer. It was his favorite place in the whole world.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.170_Text: When Mother was still walking well, and she could work, she enjoyed being on that farm. Being in the sun.//It was good to see.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.161_Text: Who am I kidding? I love it too! I love old, musty decor. Ha ha.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.126_Text: You come here to dance, don’t you? You look like the dancing type.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.26_Text: You don’t look like a busy farmer, darling.//Everything’s okay at the farm, I hope?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.147_Text: You know how it is, Farmer <PlayerName>$player</>. You’re all alone on that farm too.//<portrait=annoyed>Or do you have company?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.30_Text: You know, living alone isn’t as bad as I thought it would be.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.159_Text: You seem to always have smart insights into things.//You have broad knowledge, I noticed.
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.111_Text: Your boots are soaked! It must be raining hard outside, huh?
DT_Dialogue_Nina_Production.130_Text: “Helena, she’s just a child. It’s just a plate. We still have plenty.” Blah, blah, blah.//A monster, I was.

DT_Dialogue_Noah_Production.186_Text: *shivers* I’ve got to get my shopping done fast. It’s too cold in here.//I can’t think.
DT_Dialogue_Noah_Production.87_Text: <NPCName>Alice</> thinks there’s intelligent life in the sky, but my money is on under the water.//<portrait=normal>Did you know we’ve explored less than 20 percent of the ocean?//<portrait=surprised>There’s gotta be merfolk or something living in the other 80 percent!
DT_Dialogue_Noah_Production.80_Text: <NPCName>Frank</> and I are getting ready for the Cherry Blossom Festival.//Mama and Dad used to help make the hot pot, but we took over, even before Dad passed away.
DT_Dialogue_Noah_Production.43_Text: <NPCName>Frank</> doesn’t mind pulling long shifts. He's into it.
DT_Dialogue_Noah_Production.124_Text: <NPCName>Frank</> needs more help in Fall, so I usually work extra shifts on Sundays.
DT_Dialogue_Noah_Production.256_Text: <NpcName>Alice</> is a childhood friend. We both like talking about mysteries and picking each other’s brains.
DT_Dialogue_Noah_Production.156_Text: <NpcName>Alice</> likes to keep warm by staying active, but not me.//I’d rather bundle up in bed.
DT_Dialogue_Noah_Production.69_Text: <NpcName>Frank</> and I can’t take the weekend off. That’s when the Tavern is the busiest.
DT_Dialogue_Noah_Production.45_Text: <NpcName>Frank</> is a good cook. But not much variety, you know?//<portrait=normal>He also has this tendency to substitute ingredients.
DT_Dialogue_Noah_Production.47_Text: <NpcName>Frank</> isn’t the oldest in the family.//<portrait=normal>Aaliyah is… Four siblings total.
DT_Dialogue_Noah_Production.54_Text: <NpcName>Frank</> was born in Summer, maybe that's why he's always so chipper... Is that a thing?
DT_Dialogue_Noah_Production.38_Text: <NpcName>Theo</> gets some quick money, and we get to advertise live music at the Tavern.//<portrait=normal>People are drawn to live music for some reason.
DT_Dialogue_Noah_Production.90_Text: <PlayerName>$player</>! I saw something swimming in the distance the other day, and it was shimmering. It must have been a merperson! Wait until I tell <NPCName>Alice</> about this.//Or it could’ve been <Italic>another</> seal, like that one time…
DT_Dialogue_Noah_Production.108_Text: A couple of very well-dressed people came here last year and started taking pictures. But they weren’t acting like tourists, you see.
DT_Dialogue_Noah_Production.7_Special: A machine someplace nearby must have made the noise.
